memory_candidates.content: When removing a manifest/config key that multiple validators read, check for validators that FAIL on the key's ABSENCE, not just ones that read its contents -- and also check validators that reference the retired key's name only in COMMENTS (header docs, Rule-letter indexes) as these are easy to miss and leave stale documentation. In the agent-system routing collapse, check-extension-docs.sh's check_routing_block() hard-failed any non-exempt extension declaring provides.skills without a routing block (verify-deploy gate 3), and after deletion, 4 cslib/lean hard SKILL.md files that referenced the deleted script's name in their own provenance prose triggered a SEPARATE check (undeclared-script-reference) that was not anticipated during planning. The resulting rule: before deleting a config key or script, grep the WHOLE repo for its literal name (not just .sh files or executable callers) and triage every hit, because prose documentation referencing a soon-deleted name can itself trip a validator.

jq's pretty-printer unconditionally expands every array onto multiple lines, even when the original file hand-compacted a short array onto one line (e.g. ["a", "b", "c"]). A uniform `jq 'del(.key)' file > tmp && mv` loop across many JSON files will silently reformat any file that had such a compacted array, producing an unwanted diff beyond the intended deletion. Before applying a bulk jq-based edit across many files, spot-check each file's diff for unrelated reformatting (not just the intended key removal), and hand-rewrite via Write (preserving exact original formatting) any file where jq's default pretty-printer would mangle unrelated content.

Plan verification bullets for a multi-phase documentation-cleanup task can tighten across phases: an intermediate phase may explicitly allow 'historical mentions' of a retired name to remain (since later phases still own some of the cleanup), while a later/final phase's own verification bullet may require TRUE ZERO occurrences with no such exception. When a plan's wording shifts from 'only intentional historical mentions' to 'returns zero occurrences repo-wide', treat the stricter wording as authoritative and go back to reword even the canonical documentation's own historical-explanation prose to avoid the literal retired name (e.g. 'the former skill-level resolver' instead of naming the deleted script).
